description:
Implement the right-to-erasure path. When a user is deleted, destroying their DEK makes all encrypted personal data permanently unreadable — no need to find and delete every row. The ON DELETE CASCADE on user_encryption_keys handles DEK deletion automatically when the users row is deleted.

## What needs to happen on user deletion (in order)

  1. Revoke all bearer_tokens for the user
  2. Delete the users row
     → ON DELETE CASCADE deletes user_encryption_keys row (DEK destroyed)
     → ON DELETE CASCADE deletes subscriptions, user_flags rows
  3. The messages rows with this user_id remain in the DB but are now
     unreadable: their ciphertext cannot be decrypted without the DEK.
     This is acceptable — the data is cryptographically erased even if
     the row bytes persist.
  4. Optionally: a background cleanup job removes orphaned messages rows
     after a retention period. Not required for GDPR compliance (the
     ciphertext is meaningless without the key) but reduces storage waste.

## Gap to document: Tantivy full-text search index
  The search index stores derived content (email text snippets) that are
  NOT encrypted. Deleting the DEK does not erase these index entries.
  Options:
  A. Delete the user's index entries on account deletion (preferred — implement
     a per-user index segment deletion in TantivySearchIndex).
  B. Document the gap and accept that indexed snippets survive erasure.
  Decision deferred — document as a known gap in the erasure guarantee
  with a filed follow-up issue. Do not ship the erasure feature while
  claiming complete erasure if option B is chosen.

## Deletion endpoint
  There is currently no user deletion endpoint in stoa-mail. Implement:
    DELETE /jmap/auth/user/{username}
  Operator-only (is_operator check). Returns 204 on success.
  Emits an audit event: event.type = admin.user_deleted, username = %target.

## Test
  1. Create user, send message, verify message is readable
  2. Delete user via DELETE /jmap/auth/user/{username}
  3. Verify: users row gone, user_encryption_keys row gone
  4. Verify: messages row still exists in DB but decrypt attempt returns error
  5. Verify: audit event emitted
title: GDPR cryptographic erasure: user deletion destroys DEK and orphans encrypted data
